decisions.finding: Every quiz uses each of A-D exactly once and the guess answer is never the first option, so answers can be found by elimination
decisions.reason: Quiz and review: true of the stored keys (1-1 is [1,3,0,2]) but already fixed where the learner meets it. The player shuffles the options each time it draws a quiz or review question (site/public/js/app.js, function mcq: shuffle(q.options...)), which is what ruling R5 relies on, so re-keying would change nothing on screen. The guess: the finding stands. VIEW.guess in the same file renders the options in file order, so the position of the guess answer is visible to the learner.
decisions.change: No change to quiz or review keys. Across lessons 1-1 to 1-5 the guess answer now sits at B, D, A, C, D (it was B, D, B, B, B); 1-1's own guess is unchanged. See open questions for the player.

decisions.finding: Narration and table note say all 17 feature columns describe eight weeks of history
decisions.reason: facts data.feature_columns includes tenure_weeks (train mean 39.2 weeks, feature_stats_train), vertical, managed and three yes/no setup flags, and active_days_28 covers 28 days; advertiser 111754 in the same table has creative_refresh_days 120 (explain_examples.examples[0].row). Only the activity columns describe the eight weeks.
decisions.change: seg3 narration: 'Each row has 17 columns describing one advertiser on one date: who they are, how they are set up, and what they did in the eight weeks before.' (and '60 days after that date'). seg3 table note: 'Features: 17 columns, all known on one date. Label: what happened in the 60 days after it.'

decisions.finding: Review 1 variant 2: 'traffic-quality model' does not say which outcome a high score points to, yet the key says 0.83 resembles invalid sources
decisions.reason: A score's direction depends on which outcome is the positive one (the lesson's own glossary: 'higher means more like past positive cases'). 'Traffic quality' suggests higher = better, which would make the keyed answer wrong.
decisions.change: Stem now reads 'A model built to flag invalid traffic, trained on sources that were later confirmed valid or invalid, returns 0.83 for a new source.'

decisions.finding: Review 2 variant 1: the stem never says the model was trained on last year's leads, but the key relies on it
decisions.reason: Reproducing past outcomes is only 'the easy part' if those rows were used to fit the model; the premise has to be in the stem because each variant is shown on its own.
decisions.change: Stem now reads 'An assistant trains a lead-scoring model on last year's leads and says it "correctly reproduces the outcome of 98 percent of them".'

decisions.finding: The same question (how is a model different from my rule) is asked in the guess, quiz q1, drill 1 and the explain-back; q1 is answerable from the guess reveal
decisions.reason: Correct: q1 repeated the guess almost word for word. A question should test a consequence of the idea, not the sentence the reveal has just shown.
decisions.change: Quiz q1 rewritten (same concept, same key position): the assistant reports what the model leans on and the director asks who decided that; the keyed answer separates what training chose (columns among those supplied, cut-offs, weights) from what stayed a human choice (what churn means, which columns exist). Guess, drill and explain-back kept.

decisions.finding: seg5: 'each candidate ... adjusted until the outputs line up' leaves the mechanism as magic (I pictured every possible rule being tried)
decisions.reason: One concrete sentence removes a false picture without naming an algorithm (the outline keeps algorithms out of this lesson).
decisions.change: seg5: 'Nobody tries every possible rule. The computer starts from a rough guess, measures how far its outputs are from what really happened to thousands of past advertisers, nudges the cut-offs and weights to shrink that miss, and repeats.' One rhetorical question and the word 'simply' were cut to hold the segment at 121 words.

decisions.finding: seg6: nothing says whether a score of 0.3 may be read as a 30 percent chance
decisions.reason: The natural misreading, and the course does show later (2-4, facts calibration) that the score runs low as a percentage. SPEC rule 7 allows pointing ahead without the term.
decisions.change: seg6: 'Nor is it a percentage yet: whether 0.3 means a 30 percent chance is checked in a later lesson.' The next sentence was shortened by four words.

rulings.R1: seg1 now ends: 'So is any hand rule: block a traffic source as invalid when its click-through rate passes a line you picked, and you have built a small model too.' (general form + invalid traffic); 'and you could ship it before lunch' was cut to make room. seg2, unchanged, then states in general terms what learning adds.
rulings.R3: ask_assistant rewritten as a template, 105 words, slots: [the question, in one sentence], [units, such as advertisers, leads or creatives], [each outcome]. It still demands the row definition, row and distinct-unit counts, the label definition, the feature list without the label, example rows, and a stop before training.
rulings.R4: seg9 narration cut from 79 to 49 words, two sentences: what to ask of any model that lands on your desk, then the pointer to 1-2. Cue markers removed so the three bullets show from the start; visual unchanged.
rulings.R5: Keyed answer is the longest option in 0 of 10. Review 2 variant 3: 'Nothing more: ...' replaced by 'The same check run again on those 8,000, to confirm the match is stable' (explanation extended). Literal 'None:' / 'Nothing:' / 'Either' / 'Neither' / 'Both' options were replaced with a specific mistake. Options that accept the result FOR A STATED REASON (for example 'Trust the score: it was learned from thousands of advertisers') were kept: they are the tempting misreading the explanation argues against, not a bare 'nothing is wrong'.
rulings.R6: The most usable alternative ('keep the hand rule; it is the bar any model has to beat') sat only in other_ways. seg8 now ends: 'Meanwhile, keep your hand rule: it is the bar any model has to beat.' Two earlier sentences of seg8 were tightened to make room.
rulings.R7: Checklist items are all things the output shows; item 1 now also asks for the number of distinct units, item 3 for the full list one line each, item 4 for the label in the example rows.
